summary: Anne Hardgrove studied at Carleton College (circa 1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (circa 1991–1999). Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, she held posts at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000 and circa 2001.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Chicago (circa 1990–1996) and became Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University circa 2001.

Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Geshe Tashi Namgyal, Lambert Schmithausen, and Karin Preisendanz, and held posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield and Yutaka Hirata, holding posts at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.
Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Charles Hallisey and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, attested in 2007.

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1939–1941). A scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, she held posts at Marburg, Ankara, Bonn, and Harvard University (circa 1970–1992).
Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago from circa 1947 to 1953. Her career included an attested post at the University of Pittsburgh in 2008.

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Vienna (doctoral degree, 2002), studying under David Seyfort Ruegg and Christian Lindtner.

Annette Schmiedchen is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1985–1994) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 2000–2007), holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1995–2006) and Humboldt University (circa 2011).

Anthony C. Yu (1938–2015) studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, specializing in Sinology and religious studies. He served on the faculty at the University of Chicago from circa 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (circa 2001–2007) and served as Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison circa 2014.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (1910–1993) was a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (circa 1928–1952) and held appointments at Leiden University from 1947 through 1975.

Anthony Kennedy Warder (1924–2013) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at SOAS University of London under John Brough. He held faculty posts at the University of Edinburgh (circa 1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (circa 1964–1990).

Anthony Tribe is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Bristol and Oxford under Paul Williams, Steven Collins, and Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.
Antoine Lutz is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Meillet (1866–1936) was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in Paris under Saussure, Bréal, and Lévi, he held posts at EPHE, ENLOV, and the Collège de France (1906–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1758–1838) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He held long-term posts at ENLOV (1795–1838), the Collège de France (1806–1838), and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (1773–1832) studied under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. An Indologist, he worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, taught Persian at INALCO, and became Professor of Indian Language at the Collège de France (1815–1832).

Anton Boller (1811–1869) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. His academic career was centered at the University of Vienna, where he served as Dozent and Professor from 1845, becoming Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Sanskrit in 1855.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca (1810–1884) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1827 to 1831 and later served there as Privatdozent for oriental languages in 1849.
